v.rationale: All four pass their own suites and my probes: multi-chunk pruning of 12k rows, the report due at 06:30 UTC in winter and 05:30 UTC in summer (07:30 Copenhagen), and two schedule:run calls in the same minute dispatching only once. impl-2 is the most complete and idiomatic. It runs the prune at 03:00 Copenhagen, has coherent job lock/timeout settings and DST-aware isDue datasets, and uses modern attributes, scopes and factory states throughout. impl-3 matches it on idioms, but its prune runs on UTC with a misleading DST test, and some of its tests are weak (reflection, expect(true)). impl-1 is correct and the simplest, with a Copenhagen prune and good job settings. It loses ground on idioms: Mail::raw, inspecting the Symfony transport in tests, and checking only cron strings rather than isDue. impl-4 has a real concurrency bug. Tries(3) without FailOnTimeout, combined with UniqueFor(3600) equal to the interval, lets a slow or timed-out sync retry past its lock and overlap the next hourly run. It also adds unrequested confirm/dry-run ceremony and has a 'multiple batches' test that never runs more than one batch. To check the schedule, all four point to `php artisan schedule:list` (a cache store must be reachable). Locally that needs CACHE_STORE=array or an existing sqlite database, because the base app defaults to the database cache store.
